home.title: PreVisit Desk: your history before the visit, refills and renewals
home.desc: Answer questions in writing before a visit; the doctor gets a summary that links back to your words. Refill dates are worked out by code, and a doctor decides every renewal. A demonstration with fictional people and data.

service.title: How it works | PreVisit Desk
service.desc: Five situations: the night before a visit, a refill, a finished prescription, chest pain, and asking for a person. Who handles each step, and where the system stops.

clinicians.title: For doctors and pharmacists | PreVisit Desk
clinicians.desc: Worklist, review desk, renewal review and dispensing checks: what reaches you, which fields the system leaves blank, and the current oversight phase.

trust.title: Trust centre | PreVisit Desk
trust.desc: Twelve documents with versions and an owner: intended use, how it works, clinical safety and hazard log, human oversight, privacy, security, evaluation and regulation.

handbook.title: Health handbook | PreVisit Desk
handbook.desc: Preparing for a visit, warning signs, when to see a doctor, medicine safety. Every section names its source and the date it was checked.

emergency.title: In an emergency | PreVisit Desk
emergency.desc: In Taiwan, call 119 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of stroke, heavy bleeding or unconsciousness. If you might hurt yourself, call 1925.

home.title: Say all of it before the visit.
home.lede: Answer at home, at your own pace. What you say becomes one record the doctor can read before you walk in. You can also see when a refill opens and who a renewal is waiting for.

renewal.title: Who a renewal request passes through
renewal.body: A renewal request is not a prescription. It asks a doctor to look at a prepared record. Change the situation and see how the path changes, and who decides at each step.
renewal.label: Situation
renewal.note: In this demonstration an approved request goes to a demo pharmacy. A real prescription is written by a doctor in a visit or a telemedicine consultation.
renewal.link: Renewals and refills: the full document

stops.what: Picks the medicine, confirms how it is taken, answers the safety questions, adds recent blood pressure and glucose, reads the consent and sends it.
No rule fires, so the request joins the ordinary queue. The code ends here; it has no way to approve.
Reads the answers and readings and decides for each medicine: renew as prescribed, decline, ask for a visit, or ask for more.
Checks identity, allergies, interactions and quantity. All four must pass before it can be marked collected; otherwise it goes back or a question goes to the doctor.
Sees at every point where the request is and who it is waiting for, then collects the medicine.
Answers “not sure” to the date of the last blood test, answers the rest, and sends it.
Marks it for the doctor’s attention and lists the missing item with the rule it comes from.
Asks for the date. The request goes back to the patient with every earlier answer still there.
Adds the date and sends it again. The request returns to review.
Decides with the new information. A different dose or drug needs a visit; it cannot be changed in the system.
Answers in the safety questions that there is chest pain and breathlessness right now.
Stops. The screen shows 119 and fixed instructions, and an urgent ticket is opened outside the ordinary queue.
The ticket sits at the top of the list. Nobody is on duty here, so please call 119 yourself.
Picks a sleeping pill that is a controlled drug.
Controlled drugs are not accepted online. The item cannot be sent, and the screen says why.

patient.title: For patients
patient.body: You answer at home instead of fitting everything into the visit, and you can edit any field before sending. The AI starts from the history, medicines and allergies in your record and asks whether they are still right, rather than starting over.
patient.body2: Refill dates, where a request is, and who has looked at your data are in one place. If you want a person, “ask the doctor to contact me” is in every conversation.
patient.cta: Try it as a demo patient

physician.title: For doctors
physician.body: Before the patient walks in you see the history in order and the patient’s own readings, and every line opens the words it came from. Fields that were not asked are listed so you can ask them.
physician.body2: Assessment, plan and the note to the patient are yours; nothing is filled in for you. Every renewal is reviewed one by one. Dose and drug cannot be changed here; if they need to change, ask for a visit.

pharmacist.title: For pharmacists
pharmacist.body: Refills and renewals approved by a doctor come into one queue, each marked with its origin. You see medicines, allergies and the request itself, not the interview.
pharmacist.body2: Identity, allergies, interactions and quantity must all be ticked before anything can be marked collected. If in doubt, send it back with a reason or ask the doctor.

items.t: It does not diagnose or name an illness.
items.d: Ask “is it pneumonia?” and it is noted as a question for your doctor.

items.t: It does not prescribe, give doses, or suggest stopping or changing a medicine.
items.d: Please ask your doctor or pharmacist.
There is no such function in the code and no such button on the screen.
Nobody is watching around the clock.

items.t: It is not for real data.
items.d: Text sent to the model uses a free tier, and the provider’s terms say it may be used to improve products.

items.t: It is not connected to the National Health Insurance records or to any hospital.
items.d: It knows what the patient typed and the demo data, and nothing else.

service.title: From the night before to the medicine in hand
service.lede: The five situations below follow one fictional patient, Hsiu-Chin Lin. Each says what she does, what the system does, and where it stops and a person takes over.

previsit.title: Say it before the visit
previsit.p1: Mrs Lin has an appointment in the morning. She opens the page; the AI asks one question at a time. Her record already lists high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol and a penicillin allergy, so the AI only asks whether they are still right.
previsit.p2: At the end it reads the summary back. It is saved only after she says it is right, and she can correct any field before sending. Next morning, every line on the doctor’s screen opens her own words.
previsit.stop: She asks whether her blood pressure medicine is too strong. The AI does not answer; it notes a question for the doctor.

chat.t: Your record lists high blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol, and a penicillin allergy. Is that still right?
Yes, and I take the medicines as usual. Is the blood pressure one too strong?
That is for your doctor to judge, so I cannot answer it. I have noted it as a question for your doctor; it will be in the summary.

refill.when: A few days of medicine left
refill.title: The second fill: which day?
refill.p1: Each refillable prescription is drawn as three cells. A stamp is a fill already collected, the vertical line is today. Whether she can collect is worked out by code from the prescription dates, without AI.
refill.p2: When she can, she picks a pharmacy and a time. The pharmacist checks and prepares it and she collects it; every step shows on the request.
refill.stop: If a controlled drug is involved, symptoms changed, or she suspects a side effect, the code gives no date and sends her to a pharmacist or doctor.

steps.what: Checked by the pharmacist, being prepared
Collect it with the health card

renewal.title: Asking the doctor about a renewal
renewal.p1: Another prescription is finished. She picks the medicine, confirms how she takes it, answers the safety questions, adds recent blood pressure and glucose, reads the consent and sends it. If she closes the page halfway, the answers are kept and she can go on from her phone.
renewal.p2: The rule engine gives each medicine one of five results. They only change what the doctor sees first. Then the doctor decides, item by item.
renewal.stop: The code does not approve. After the doctor agrees, the prescription itself is still written in a visit or a telemedicine consultation.
renewal.table: The five results of the rule engine

When

rows: One answer needs a look, or a reading is out of date

Pregnancy, a recent hospital stay, changed symptoms

redflag.title: Rules come before AI, and they stop everything
redflag.p1: Every message goes through the red-flag rules before the AI. On a match the AI is not called at all: the screen shows fixed text and phone numbers, and an urgent ticket opens in the doctors’ workspace.
redflag.p2: This step runs first in the middle of an interview, after sending, and while a person has taken over.
redflag.stop: The system does not make the call. She, or someone with her, has to dial 119.

chat.t: Sudden strong chest pain, cold sweat
What you describe may need care right away. Call 119 now, or ask someone near you to call.

handover.title: The person has a name, and the AI steps back
handover.p1: She presses “ask the doctor to contact me”. Once a care coordinator takes over, the AI stops replying and the person continues in the same conversation, with name and title on every message.
handover.p2: When it is settled they can close it or hand the conversation back to the AI.
handover.stop: Nobody is on duty here. If it is urgent, do not wait for a reply; make the call.

chat.t: I stopped the medicine for a few days. How should I take it now?
How to take it is for a doctor or pharmacist to say. I have told the care team.
Ya-Wen Hsu, care coordinator, has taken over. The AI is paused.
Hello Mrs Lin, this is Ya-Wen, the care coordinator. I am asking the doctor to look at your medicines. How many days do you have left?

end.title: Walk through it yourself
end.body: Pick a demo patient; all five situations can be tried.

clinicians.title: For doctors, pharmacists and care coordinators
clinicians.lede: The system does one job: put what the patient said in order and bring it to the person who should read it. Judgement, signature and dispensing stay with you.

desk.title: Review desk
desk.p1: On the left, the patient’s record, medicines and earlier visits. In the middle, the subjective (S) the AI put in order and the patient’s own readings (O). On the right, your writing. Every line in the middle opens the original words and can be edited; an edited line keeps who changed it and what it said before.
desk.p2: Assessment (A), plan (P) and the note to the patient start empty. The system suggests nothing and offers no differential. Drafts save with versions; signing locks the note, and corrections go in as addenda. The patient sees your note only after you sign.

desk.sTitle: Subjective (S), ordered by AI from the interview
desk.author: Dr Po-Yu Chen

desk.missing: What makes it worse: not asked yet

queue.title: What comes first
queue.p1: The worklist is ordered by urgency and due time, not by a model’s opinion. Urgent has one source: a red-flag rule, or a dangerous symptom answered in a renewal. The model cannot open an urgent ticket.
rows: A red flag, or a dangerous symptom right now in a renewal
On top, with its own red count
Past the set handling time without a decision
Previsits and renewals that were sent
Returns to review when the patient replies
head: List
How it gets there
Order and marking
queue.caption: How the worklist is sorted

renewal.title: Renewal review
renewal.p1: Each request shows the engine’s result, which rules fired and where they come from, the patient’s answers and the trend of readings. Each medicine is decided on its own: renew, decline, visit required, or ask for more.
renewal.p2: Dose and drug cannot be changed here. If they need to change, choose “visit required”. Agreement between your decisions and the engine is shown on the oversight page, by drug class.

phase.title: Oversight phase
phase.p1: This is phase {{phase}}: a doctor reviews every renewal request. No button raises the phase, and no code approves automatically.
phase.p2: Phases two and three exist only as conditions: 250 doctor decisions per drug class, agreement above a threshold published beforehand, ethics review and the regulator’s consent, and an institution and a named doctor who carry responsibility. Given what this project is, none of them is met.

coordinator.title: Care coordinators
coordinator.p1: Can assign, contact patients, take over conversations, manage tags and follow-up, and write internal notes. Cannot sign a note or decide a renewal.

pharmacy.title: Pharmacists
pharmacy.p1: The queue holds two kinds of case: refills of an existing prescription, and renewals a doctor approved. Each is marked with its origin. You see medicines, allergies and the request; not the interview or the doctor’s note.
pharmacy.p2: “Complete” works only when all four checks are ticked. If one is in doubt, send it back with a reason or ask the doctor. Try leaving one out.
pharmacy.figure: Excerpt of the dispensing check, fictional data

items.label: Directions
items.value: 50 mg, one tablet once a day after breakfast

pharmacy.done: All four are checked; it can be completed.

log.title: Reading leaves a record
log.p1: Every time you open a patient’s data, the time, your name and role, and what you viewed are written down. If that cannot be written, the data is not shown. The patient can see it on their privacy page.

missing.title: What is not here
items: No connection to national medication records or a hospital system; medicines come from the patient and the demo data.
No image or lab report upload, and no physical examination.
No diagnostic or drug suggestions, and no interaction database.
No protocol approved by a doctor or pharmacist. The rule file says so itself.
No workload limit, and nothing that notices a review done too fast. This is listed as a known gap.

enter.title: See the real screens
enter.p1: The author gives out the passwords of the demo doctor, pharmacist, coordinator and administrator accounts. Without one, start with a demo patient.

trust.title: Trust centre
trust.lede: Twelve documents on how this system works, where it can go wrong, and who is responsible when it does. What has not been done is written down too.
trust.reviewNote: No external clinical review has taken place. No doctor, pharmacist or organisation endorses these documents.

emergency.title: In an emergency
emergency.lede: Call first, then do the rest. This site does not call an ambulance for you, and nobody is waiting behind it. The numbers below work in Taiwan.
emergency.crisisTitle: Thinking of hurting yourself, or someone near you is
emergency.crisisBody: 1925 is free and answered day and night, all year. Lifeline 1995 and Teacher Chang 1980 can also be called; their hours are announced by each organisation. If someone is hurt or in danger now, call 119.
emergency.whenTitle: Call 119 or go to an emergency department for

when.t: Chest pain or tightness with cold sweat or breathlessness
Face drooping, weakness on one side, slurred speech
Trouble breathing, blue lips or nails
Tight throat, swollen face, rash and breathlessness after food or medicine
Vomiting blood, or black stool with dizziness and cold sweat
Sudden severe headache, confusion, cannot be woken

emergency.whenNote: From chapter 2 of the handbook (in Chinese), where every section names a government or hospital source. If something is not listed, that does not mean it can wait; if you are worried, call.
say: Say where first: address, crossing, floor or a landmark.
Say what happened, since when, and whether the person is awake.
Mention long-term illnesses, current medicines and allergies.
Stay on the line and follow the instructions.
Send someone to the door; take the health card and medicine bags along.
site: If a warning sign is mentioned in any conversation, the rules stop the interview and show fixed text and phone numbers, without calling the AI.
An urgent ticket opens in the demo doctors’ workspace. Nobody gets a phone call.
Red-flag checks keep working when the AI is off or its quota is used up.
